text: {"verdict": "supported", "answer": "The CheA(3)/CheY(6) chemotaxis study shows that specificity is structurally encoded: a methionine finger (with an adjacent alanine) present only in cognate regulators mediates complex formation and enables rapid phosphotransfer from CheA(3)-P, and transplanting these residues into noncognate CheYs both changed their specificity and allowed rapid phosphotransfer. This directly links histidine kinase/response-regulator specificity determinants to rapid phosphotransfer.
